slides.title: Why is your *report so slow*?
slides.voiceover: Your report takes minutes? Look for this one line.
slides.spoken: Your report takes minutes? Look for this one line.

slides.heading: The *mistake*
slides.left:
LOOP AT lt_orders INTO DATA(ls).
  SELECT SINGLE name1 FROM kna1
    WHERE kunnr = @ls-kunnr
    INTO @DATA(lv_name).
ENDLOOP.
slides.right:
SELECT kunnr, name1 FROM kna1
  FOR ALL ENTRIES IN @lt_orders
  WHERE kunnr = @lt_orders-kunnr
  INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_kna1).
slides.voiceover: A SELECT inside a loop calls the database once per row. FOR ALL ENTRIES reads them all in one go.
slides.spoken: A SELECT inside a loop calls the database once per row. FOR ALL ENTRIES reads them all in one go.

slides.label: THE FIX
slides.heading: 10,000 orders = ?
slides.voiceover: Ten thousand orders in a loop: ten thousand calls. For all entries needs just one.
slides.spoken: Ten thousand orders in a loop: ten thousand calls. FOR ALL ENTRIES needs just one.

slides.label: REMEMBER
slides.heading: Check it's *not empty*
slides.body: IF lt_orders IS NOT INITIAL first. An empty table makes FOR ALL ENTRIES read every row.
slides.voiceover: One catch: check the table isn't empty first, or it reads every row. Save this.
slides.spoken: One catch: check the table isn't empty first, or it reads every row. Save this.

posts.caption:
Your report takes minutes? Look for a SELECT inside a LOOP.

1. SELECT SINGLE inside LOOP AT = one database call per row
2. Read everything once with FOR ALL ENTRIES IN (or a JOIN), then READ TABLE inside the loop
3. Always check IF lt_orders IS NOT INITIAL first: an empty driver table makes FOR ALL ENTRIES read the whole table

Never created a domain? Do it click by click.

Domain, Part 4 of 11: create a domain in SE11.

1. SE11: select Domain, enter a Z/Y name (e.g. ZD_PRIORITY), click Create
2. Enter a short description
3. Definition tab: data type (e.g. CHAR) and number of characters
4. Save: a package + transport request, or Local Object ($TMP) for tests
5. Check, then activate (Ctrl+F3)
